The problem

The model does not know where your order is, but it will answer confidently

Without tools
QuestionWhere is order 417 right now?Model answer“Your order 417 is on its way and will arrive tomorrow morning.”
Not a single lookup in the delivery system. Sounds convincing, but it is a guess.
With a tool · Google AI Studio, captured 16.10.2026
A tool is a function of your system the model can ask to call. The model asked for the order data (violet), got it (amber) and answered from it (green).

A tool

A function declaration: a name, a description, parameters. That is all the model sees

AI Studio → Run settings → Tools → Function calling → Edit

GenAI Basics • Lesson 11 • Function calling and agents08 / 21
Description

The model picks a tool by its description. Write it like a task for an intern

✗ Weak
get_data
"Gets data."
Which data? When to call it? The model has to guess.
✓ Good
get_order_status
"Current status, courier and arrival time of ONE delivery order by its number. Use when the customer asks where an order is."
What it does, what for and when to call it. One tool, one job.
If two tools sound alike (get_order and find_order), the model will mix them up. Rename or merge them.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 11 • Function calling and agents09 / 21
Agent

An agent = a model + tools + a loop until the task is done

1
Model thinks
2
Picks a tool
3
The program runs it
4
Result goes back
get_order_status
no tool needed
Final answer
limit:
5 steps
Goal:
answer the customer
Steps 1→4 repeat: the model may call several tools in a row, as Claude did on slide 3.
The loop ends when the model needs no more tools: it writes the final answer.
A step limit is a must: without it an agent can go round in circles and burn money.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 11 • Function calling and agents10 / 21
Code (reference)

In code the library runs the loop: a function plus its docstring

Python, the google-genai library (as in L03)
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> dict:
    """Current status and arrival time of one delivery order."""
    return {"status": "on the way", "courier": "Anna", "eta_minutes": 12}

client = genai.Client()          # key from GEMINI_API_KEY
r = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    contents="Where is order 417?",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(tools=[get_order_status]))
print(r.text)
The docstring is the tool description for the model.
tools=[…] — pass a plain Python function. The library calls it and hands the result back to the model.
OpenAI and Anthropic work the same way with different field names. Code is optional for the homework.

Local models can call functions too, but they make more mistakes

Tool-capable in Ollama and LM Studio, October 2026
Qwen3.5
0.8 to 122 billion parameters
small sizes fit a laptop
Granite 4.2
3, 8 and 30 billion parameters
small sizes fit a laptop
gpt-oss-20b
≈ 16 GB memory
needs a strong laptop or PC
The same idea locally: localhost:1234 (LM Studio) and localhost:11434 (Ollama) accept OpenAI-format tools. Use the openai library, as in L10, not google-genai.
A small model more often picks the wrong tool or argument format. Start with 1–2 simple functions and test.

Hands-on with an agent

A coding agent can build your first agent from one prompt

Prompt for a coding agent: Codex in ChatGPT or Antigravity (free, with limits), Claude Code (paid)
Build a small Python support agent for a courier service. Synthetic data only.
1. Two functions: get_order_status(order_id) and create_return(order_id, reason), data from orders.json (5 orders).
2. Run create_return only after I confirm in the console (y/n).
3. Model: Gemini 3.8 Flash via google-genai, at most 5 calls per question.
4. Log every call: time, function, arguments, result.
5. Show 3 example dialogues and what is in the log.
The prompt already has every rule of the lesson: narrow functions, confirmation for the risky action, a step limit, a log.
You need your own Gemini API key (free tier with a daily limit: AI Studio → Get API key; enough for 3–4 test dialogues).

GenAI Basics • Lesson 11 • Function calling and agents15 / 21
Risks

Tools give the model hands. The main risk is someone else’s text giving it orders

Prompt injection
a fetched page or email says “transfer the money” — the model may obey
Action without asking
the agent sent an email or created a refund on its own
Endless loop
the agent goes round in circles burning money
Too much access
the support bot can delete orders
Defences live in code
✓least privilege for every tool
✓a human confirms actions with consequences
✓step and money limits
✓a log of every call
✓tool results are data, not commands

GenAI Basics • Lesson 11 • Function calling and agents17 / 21
Rules

Four rules make an agent safer

1
The model proposes
Narrow tools
one function, one job, a clear description
▶
2
The program checks
Checks in code
the program checks arguments and rights, not the model
▶
3
A human confirms
Confirmation for risk
money, emails, deletion only after a “yes”
▶
4
The log records
Limits and a log
steps, budget, a record of every call
What the log looks like (example)
12:04:31  get_order_status(order_id="523")  → ok           step 2/5 · $0.002
12:04:33  create_return(order_id="523")     → waiting for an operator’s “yes”
This is also the homework grading checklist.

Homework

Homework: design an agent’s tools and test them in AI Studio

  1. Pick a work task for an agent (support, warehouse, HR…)
  2. Describe 2–3 functions: name, description, parameters
  3. Repeat the AI Studio demo with your functions and synthetic data
  4. Test 5 questions: which call the model proposed, and was it right
  5. Describe the risks: where the confirmation goes, what limit, what is logged
